A click on a plain `<a>` makes the browser load the whole next page: new HTML, new scripts, and all client state is gone. `Link` from `next/link` changes the page in the browser and fetches the code of the next page ahead of time.

The rule reports an `<a>` with an `href` that is a plain string and points inside the site, such as `/about` or `about`. It does not look at which pages exist, so a link to an API route or to a file in `public/` is reported too.

These are allowed: an `href` with a scheme (`https:`, `mailto:`, `tel:`), one that starts with `//` or `#`, an element with `target="_blank"`, and an element with `download`.

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad */}
```jsx
export default function Nav() {
  return <a href="/about">About</a>;
}
```

{/* bad */}
```jsx
export default function LogOut() {
  return <a href="/api/logout">Log out</a>;
}
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```jsx
import Link from "next/link";

export default function Nav() {
  return <Link href="/about">About</Link>;
}
```

{/* good */}
```jsx
export default function Footer() {
  return (
    <footer>
      <a href="https://example.com">Partner site</a>
      <a href="mailto:hello@example.com">Write to us</a>
      <a href="#top">Back to top</a>
      <a href="/terms" target="_blank">Terms</a>
      <a href="/price-list.pdf" download>Price list</a>
    </footer>
  );
}
```
